when: Measures a monotonic relationship between two variables using ranks, robust to outliers and skew.
example: You rank ten films by budget and by box-office takings. Spearman's correlation measures whether higher-budget films tend to earn more, even when the pattern is not a straight line.
small_sample: A robust small-sample choice. Report a bootstrap confidence interval, and prefer Kendall's tau when tied ranks are common.
assumptions: Both variables are at least ordinal
The relationship is monotonic, rising or falling consistently
alternative: Kendall's tau, when the sample is small or ranks contain many ties

# survey_skeleton.R
# StatChooser sample survey skeleton (surveyframe method = "correlation_spearman").
# Section A is a standard demographic block. Section B, and C/D/E where present,
# carry the measures the analysis plan needs. Replace every [bracketed] stem
# with your own validated items before fielding the survey.
# install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)

# ---- Choice sets (define once, reuse) ----
agree5 <- sf_choices("agree5", 1:5,
  c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"))
gender_cs <- sf_choices("gender_cs",
  c("woman", "man", "nonbinary", "selfdescribe", "na"),
  c("Woman", "Man", "Non-binary", "Prefer to self-describe", "Prefer not to say"))
edu_cs <- sf_choices("edu_cs", 1:5,
  c("Secondary or below", "Diploma", "Bachelor degree", "Master degree", "Doctorate"))
role_cs <- sf_choices("role_cs", 1:4,
  c("Entry or junior", "Mid-level", "Senior or manager", "Executive or owner"))
industry_cs <- sf_choices("industry_cs", 1:5,
  c("Manufacturing", "Retail or trade", "Services", "Public sector", "Other"))

# ---- Section A: Respondent profile ----
sec_a <- sf_item("sec_a", "Section A: Respondent profile", type = "section_break",
  section_intro = "A few background questions about you.")
age <- sf_item("age", "Your age in years", type = "numeric")
gender <- sf_item("gender", "Your gender", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "gender_cs")
education <- sf_item("education", "Highest level of education completed", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "edu_cs")
job_role <- sf_item("job_role", "Your role or seniority", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "role_cs")
experience <- sf_item("experience", "Years of experience", type = "numeric")
industry <- sf_item("industry", "Your industry or sector", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "industry_cs")

# ---- Section B: The two variables ----
sec_b <- sf_item("sec_b", "Section B: The two variables", type = "section_break")
x_var_1 <- sf_item("x_var_1", "[Variable X item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "x_var")
x_var_2 <- sf_item("x_var_2", "[Variable X item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "x_var")
x_var_3 <- sf_item("x_var_3", "[Variable X item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "x_var")
x_var <- sf_scale("x_var", "Variable X", c("x_var_1", "x_var_2", "x_var_3"), method = "mean")
y_var_1 <- sf_item("y_var_1", "[Variable Y item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "y_var")
y_var_2 <- sf_item("y_var_2", "[Variable Y item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "y_var")
y_var_3 <- sf_item("y_var_3", "[Variable Y item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "y_var")
y_var <- sf_scale("y_var", "Variable Y", c("y_var_1", "y_var_2", "y_var_3"), method = "mean")

# ---- Analysis plan (ids match the items and scales above) ----
plan_entry <- list(
  id                = "RQ1",
  research_question = "Is there a monotonic relationship between X and Y?",
  family            = "association",
  method            = "correlation_spearman",
  roles             = list(
    x          = "x_var",
    y          = "y_var"
  ),
  options           = list(alpha = 0.05)
)

# ---- Assemble the instrument ----
instr <- sf_instrument(
  title         = "[Your study title]",
  description   = "[Population and purpose]",
  components    = list(
    sec_a, age, gender, education, job_role, experience, industry, sec_b, x_var_1, x_var_2, x_var_3, x_var, y_var_1, y_var_2, y_var_3, y_var
  ),
  analysis_plan = list(plan_entry)
)
